headline: A 2013 federal law that tightens rules on compounded drugs and creates a system to trace prescription drugs through the supply chain.
what_it_does: The law sets new federal oversight for compounding pharmacies and outsourcing facilities that make custom drugs. Registered outsourcing facilities must report what they make, submit adverse event reports, face risk-based inspections, and pay fees. Separately, it requires drug makers, wholesalers, dispensers, and repackagers to pass along transaction records and mark packages so prescription drugs can be traced, with package-level tracing starting ten years after enactment. It also sets federal licensing standards for wholesalers and third-party logistics providers and overrides certain state and local rules on those topics.

who_it_affects.how: They must register annually, report compounded drugs and adverse events, accept inspections, and pay establishment and reinspection fees if they operate as registered outsourcing facilities.
They must affix product identifiers to packages and provide transaction history at each change of ownership.

who_it_affects.group: Wholesale drug distributors and third-party logistics providers
who_it_affects.how: They must verify trading partners, investigate suspect products, handle illegitimate products, and meet new federal licensing standards.

They must keep transaction information and, once package-level tracing begins, meet additional tracing requirements, with a possible exemption route for dispensers with 25 or fewer full-time employees.

who_it_affects.group: Patients who receive compounded or prescription drugs
who_it_affects.how: Compounded drugs must meet new safety and labeling rules, and the law aims to make it easier to trace and recall tainted or counterfeit medicines.
They must send the federal government reports on disciplinary actions, recalls, and concerns about compounding pharmacies.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 27, 2013; the compounding provisions and many supply chain provisions took effect on the timelines set in the law, and package-level tracing requirements take effect ten years after enactment, around November 2023.
